title: ouya.tv, from “pre-order” to “shutting down”
lede: Screenshots of ouya.tv as the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine saved it, kept here as images. Click one to open the original capture.[^34]

snips.text: “**Cracking open the last closed platform: the TV.**”
“Once you’re in—it takes just **$99**—every game on OUYA is **free to try**, free to love and absolutely free to brag about.”
“**1112** games and counting”, with tiles for “OUYA in China” and controller faceplates at $9.99 each.
“**NOTICE: This website will be shutting down on June 25, 2019.**”

note: Embedded videos in these pages were not archived and show as empty boxes. The home page counter was drawn by a script; the July 2013 capture shows it mid-animation, so we do not use that reading as a figure.

captures.label: Pre-order
captures.title: The day the campaign closed
captures.text: A single page: “Pre-order OUYA now,” the slogan and a sign-up box. The Kickstarter page sent latecomers here.[^1]
captures.warn: The video in the white box was not archived.

captures.title: Two weeks after the retail launch
captures.text: The product photograph, the price and the free-to-try promise. NPD’s “relatively light” assessment came nine days later.[^12]

captures.label: Sold
captures.title: Two weeks after Razer confirmed the deal
captures.text: A busier page: 1,112 games, a forum, “OUYA in China,” and accessories on sale. The console itself is no longer the centerpiece.[^25]

captures.label: Notice
captures.title: Twenty-three days to go
captures.text: The same page as in 2015 with a black banner across the top and the counter at 1,250.[^30]
